<description>
`outscript=VALUE:SCRIPT[:FLAGS]` only reads the flags when there are exactly three fields (bitcoin-tx.cpp:482). With a trailing or extra `:` the flags are silently dropped:

```
$ bitcoin-tx -create outscript=0:OP_DROP:S nversion=1
010000000001000000000000000017a91471ed53322d470bb96657deb786b94f97dd46fb158700000000  # P2SH, as requested
$ bitcoin-tx -create outscript=0:OP_DROP:S: nversion=1
0100000000010000000000000000017500000000  # bare OP_DROP output, exit code 0
```

So a typo gives a transaction paying to the raw script instead of the P2SH/P2WSH wrapper, with no error. `outpubkey` and `outaddr` already reject extra fields with "TX output missing or too many separators".

This rejects `outscript` arguments with more than three fields, and `in=TXID:VOUT[:SEQUENCE_NUMBER]` arguments with more than three fields (which were accepted the same way), both with a general "Invalid format, expected ..." error. `bitcoin-util-test.json` gets a case for each; they fail on master (exit code 0) and pass with the fix, and `tool_utils.py` passes.

AI tools were used to help find this issue and to prepare the patch and test.
</description>

<commits>
2fef1db4f8 bitcoin-tx: reject in and outscript arguments with too many separators

outscript=VALUE:SCRIPT[:FLAGS] and in=TXID:VOUT[:SEQUENCE_NUMBER] only
checked for too few fields and silently ignored extra ones, so a typo like
outscript=0:OP_DROP:S: dropped the P2SH flag without an error. Reject both
with a general "Invalid format" error.
</commits>
